title: Is this just a token eater?
author: Benhamish-WH-Allen
selftext: It’s non stop generation. Maybe a few hours to generate the foundation and then time spent details, endless polishing? It leads to Exponential context growth? Will it reach a limit and just say nope can’t add anything else? or will it just hallucinate at the end?

comments.author: Yenii_3025
comments.body: I once put my dick in a flute.

comments.author: nayheyxus
comments.body:
Though I'm not sure what you're working with; It can certainly seem that way, but it depends on your work flow.  
  
If you expect perfection from AI, then it will become nonstop regeneration. 

What works for me, is build portion of the game and get it to working/usable, document what you would like to improve upon, but move on.   
  
This keeps you from wasting credits trying to polish something using a chaos sponge, what I've found, is when I want to go back to polish something, its far easier because I have other aspects in place. I also have a better understanding of how it should look/operate.

replies.author: Benhamish-WH-Allen
replies.body:
I have google ultra and about to run out. It’s just so much wasted context. Planning out to agentic loop is just even more context. I suppose it’s just about the machines you have access to.

At the moment I’m trying to get llm output into a database that does not have an entry for what the llm is talking about.

replies.author: Hello_im_a_dog
replies.body:
What is your final objective? Commercially successful titles? Or build something that you'll find fun? Based on that you can develop your harness accordingly. 

For example, a few colleagues of mine in India are doing quite well making commercially successful titles with minimal operational expenditure (opex). None of them could be called art, given that they are reskins of existing popular  indie titles. But they have achieved their objective.

replies.author: Benhamish-WH-Allen
replies.body:
lol final objective? instilling empathy into a bunch of powdered rocks. I did try an agentic loop for one project but for this one it’s a lot of unique prompts. The time to process prompts just increases as the context grows, it runs 30-50 second unit tests after each prompt. I don’t mind that it’s checking but it seems overkill. 

I always say I’ll remake this into a better structure but just one more prompt first. But even with a harness wouldn’t it become bloat at some point?

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: Not sure why you want to go full agentic for gamedev. Yeah, I think you are wasting token

replies.author: Benhamish-WH-Allen
replies.body: I’m sure I am wasting tokens. I’m hoping my 5090 will handle agentic next year or maybe a 6090.I was reading that 50% or more tokens are wasted globally. For the agentic stuff It seems to me that once the game is built you can say reskin that thing and a few hours later you have another game. But won’t adding features to that game just make you start with a bloated context window?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I have no idea. I just prompt every 5-10min and it has been fast enough for me. I am still getting a lot of done in 1-2 week intervals instead of 3-5 weeks+ 

unless you have a way to turn in these games for a profit, I feel like you are just running at a loss even if you can reskin a game every few hours.

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: It won't tell you it is done. As with art in any other condition, you as the artist decide when the art ends. If you expect this to be a "here's a prompt spit out the end result," you should likely choose a different hobby.
